title: Tech Note: At the Core of the Data: The Address Table and Bit Table
author: Olivier Deschanels
featured_technology: Byte swapping between Mac and Windows integer/longint storage
Primary Address Table (PAT) / Secondary Address Table (SAT)
APPLY TO SELECTION for forcing platform re-save

historical_commentary.text: Olivier Deschanels (4D S.A.) continues from TN 01-29 to explain how 4D's classic engine locates records within its single 128-byte-block data file using a two-level Primary/Secondary Address Table structure, how a record's 4-byte 'tag' encodes both the 4D version and originating platform (Mac vs. Windows) to control byte-swapping, and how a separate bit-table tracks free vs. occupied blocks for allocation. This deep-dive into 4D's classic .4DD/.data file internals describes the storage engine used prior to 4D's move to the 4D SQL/CoreData engine (4D v11 SQL onward, and 4D v12+ compiled architecture), which changed the underlying storage format; the specific address-table/bit-table mechanics described no longer apply to the current 4D engine, making this note of historical/archival interest for understanding legacy 4D data files rather than a guide to current internals.
related_updates: 4D replaced its classic data-file engine with the 4D SQL/CoreData storage engine starting around 4D v11 SQL (2007), changing the internal record/address/bit-table structures described here
Developers working with legacy pre-v11 .4DD/.data files for recovery purposes may still find this architecture description useful as historical reference
APPLY TO SELECTION remains a valid current 4D command, though its use here (forcing platform-native record re-save) is no longer a relevant optimization on the current engine
